## Workstation stack

- **Base** (Minimal Fedora, debloated GNOME)
- **Dev** (Visual Studio Code, Git + LFS, Python, Docker, SSH)
- **Research** (Quarto, LaTeX, Pandoc tooling, Obsidian)
- **Documents** (Okular, OCR, GROBID, Recoll)
- **Sync & Backup** (Nextcloud, Vorta/Borg)
- **Productivity & Media** (Thunderbird, Chrome, GIMP, Audacity, OBS Studio)
- **Security** (KeePassXC, ClamAV)

## Eduroam

On Fedora with GNOME, open **Settings → Wi-Fi**, select **eduroam**, and use the following settings:

| Setting              | Value                          |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| Wi-Fi security       | WPA & WPA2 Enterprise          |
| Authentication       | Protected EAP (PEAP)           |
| Anonymous identity   | Leave blank                    |
| CA certificate       | **No CA certificate required** |
| PEAP version         | Automatic                      |
| Inner authentication | MSCHAPv2                       |
| Username             | Frankfurt School username      |
| Password             | Frankfurt School password      |

For **FS employees**, the username is `name@fs.de`, where `name` is the Windows login (without `@fs.de`). This is not necessarily the employee's email address.

Fedora may show a warning when selecting **No CA certificate required**; confirm this choice. After entering your credentials, click **Connect**. Fedora/NetworkManager normally stores the connection profile, so you only need to enter these settings once.
